answer: Pairwise-bounded settlement: when the contract converts attestations into weight, it takes each pair of endorsers i and j and counts the targets both vouched for. Past the quorum threshold that pair counts as one unit, its weight the larger of the two, not the sum, so their cluster is one island whose zenith is a single identity's pull; when a member is slashed the ripple hits every identity in that island. A farmer with 1,000 puppets pays 1,000 fees, no bulk discount, and still draws one unit of weight, so cost climbs with N while the payoff stays flat. The honest user pays once.
